spots.name: Florence Cathedral

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Florence Cathedral, formally the Cathedral of Saint Mary of the Flower, is the cathedral of the Catholic Archdiocese of Florence in Florence, Italy.

spots.name: David
spots.summary: David is a masterpiece of Italian Renaissance sculpture in marble created from 1501 to 1504 by Michelangelo.

spots.name: Uffizi

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Uffizi Gallery is a prominent art museum adjacent to the Piazza della Signoria in the Historic Centre of Florence in the region of Tuscany, Italy. One of the most important Italian museums and the most visited, it is also one of the largest and best-known in the world.

spots.name: Palazzo Vecchio

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo Vecchio is the town hall of Florence, Italy. It overlooks the Piazza della Signoria, which holds a copy of Michelangelo's David statue, and the gallery of statues in the adjacent Loggia dei Lanzi.

spots.name: Palazzo Pitti

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Palazzo Pitti, in English sometimes called the Pitti Palace, is a vast, mainly in the Renaissance style, palace in Florence, Italy. It is situated on the south side of the River Arno, a short distance from the Ponte Vecchio.

spots.name: Ponte Vecchio
spots.summary: The Ponte Vecchio is a medieval stone closed-spandrel segmental arch bridge over the Arno, in Florence, Italy. The only bridge in Florence spared from destruction during World War II, it is noted for the shops built along it; building shops on such bridges was once a common practice.

spots.name: Piazza della Signoria
spots.summary: Piazza della Signoria is a W-shaped square in front of the Palazzo Vecchio in Florence, Central Italy. It was named after the Palazzo della Signoria, also called Palazzo Vecchio.

spots.name: Florence Baptistery
spots.summary: The Florence Baptistery, also known as the Baptistery of Saint John, is a religious building in Florence, Italy. Dedicated to the patron saint of the city, John the Baptist, it has been a focus of religious, civic, and artistic life since its completion.

spots.name: Perseus with the Head of Medusa
spots.summary: Perseus with the Head of Medusa is a bronze sculpture made by Benvenuto Cellini in the period 1545–1554. The sculpture stands on a square base which has bronze relief panels depicting the story of Perseus and Andromeda, similar to a predella on an altarpiece.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Perseus with the Head of Medusa

spots.name: Santa Maria Novella

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Santa Maria Novella is a Dominican church in Florence. It is considered the most important Romano-Gothic church in Tuscany and is a World Heritage Site. Its construction started in 1290 and it took almost 200 years to be completed. It was consecrated in 1420.

spots.name: Vasari Corridor

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Vasari Corridor is a 16th-century elevated enclosed passageway in Florence, connecting the Palazzo Vecchio with the Palazzo Pitti. It was designed by, and named for, architect Giorgio Vasari to allow Duke Cosimo I de' Medici to move undisturbed between both palaces.

spots.name: Santa Croce, Florence

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica di Santa Croce is a minor basilica and the principal Franciscan church of Florence, Italy. It is situated on the Piazza di Santa Croce, about 800 metres (2,600 ft) southeast of the Duomo, on what was once marshland beyond the city walls.

spots.name: Galleria dell'Accademia

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Galleria dell'Accademia di Firenze is an art museum in Florence, in Tuscany in central Italy. It houses the Michelangelo sculpture David and other sculptures by Michelangelo, and a large collection of paintings by Florentine artists, mostly from the period 1300–1600.

spots.name: Palazzo Medici Riccardi

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo Medici, also called the Palazzo Medici Riccardi after the later family that acquired and expanded it, is a 15th-century Renaissance palace in Florence, Italy. It was built for the Medici family, who dominated the politics of the Republic of Florence.

spots.name: Abduction of a Sabine Woman
spots.summary: Abduction of a Sabine Woman is a large and complex marble statue by the Flemish sculptor and architect Giambologna. It was completed between 1579 and 1583 for Francesco I de' Medici, Grand Duke of Tuscany. Giambologna achieved widespread fame in his lifetime, and this work is often considered his masterpiece.

spots.name: Giotto's Campanile
spots.summary: Giotto's Campanile is a free-standing campanile that is part of the complex of buildings that make up Florence Cathedral on the Piazza del Duomo in Florence, Italy.

spots.name: Basilica of San Lorenzo

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Basilica di San Lorenzo is one of the largest churches of Florence, Italy, situated at the centre of the main market district of the city, and it is the burial place of all the principal members of the Medici family from Cosimo il Vecchio to Cosimo III.

spots.name: Fountain of Neptune
spots.summary: The Fountain of Neptune is situated in the Piazza della Signoria in Florence, Italy, near the northwest corner of the Palazzo Vecchio.

spots.name: Loggia dei Lanzi
spots.summary: The Loggia dei Lanzi, also called the Loggia della Signoria, is a building on the south corner of the Piazza della Signoria in Florence, Italy, adjoining the Uffizi Gallery, and diagonally to the east the Palazzo della Signoria, the political center of the city.

spots.name: Santissima Annunziata

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica della Santissima Annunziata is a Renaissance-style, Catholic minor basilica in Florence, region of Tuscany, Italy. This is considered the mother church of the Servite Order. It is located at the northeastern side of the Piazza Santissima Annunziata near the city center.

spots.name: Bargello
spots.summary: The Bargello, also known as the Palazzo del Bargello or Palazzo del Popolo, is a former public building and police headquarters, later a prison, in Florence, Italy. Mostly built in the 13th century, since 1865 it has housed the Museo Nazionale del Bargello, a national art museum.

spots.name: Historic Centre of Florence
spots.summary: The historic centre of Florence is part of quartiere 1 of the Italian city of Florence. This quarter was named a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1982.

spots.name: Museo dell'Opera del Duomo
spots.summary: The Museo dell'Opera del Duomo in Florence, Italy is a museum containing many of the original works of art created for Florence Cathedral, including the adjacent Florence Baptistery and Giotto's campanile.

spots.name: Piazza del Duomo
spots.summary: Piazza del Duomo is located in Florence, Tuscany, Italy. It is one of the most visited places in Europe and the world and in Florence, the most visited area of the city. The Piazza del Duomo is part of the Historic Centre of Florence, which was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982.

spots.name: Medici Chapels

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Medici Chapels are two chapels built between the 16th and 17th centuries as an extension to the Basilica of San Lorenzo, in the Italian city of Florence. They are the Sagrestia Nuova, designed by Michelangelo, and the larger Cappella dei Principi, a collaboration between the Medici family and architects.

spots.name: Orsanmichele

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Orsanmichele, Or San Michele or Orsammichele is a communal building and church in the Italian city of Florence. Its uniqueness as an architectural construction lies not only in its multifunctionality as grain market, granary and oratory.

spots.name: Piazzale Michelangelo
spots.summary: Piazzale Michelangelo is a square with a panoramic view of Florence, Italy, located in the Oltrarno district.

spots.name: Hercules and Cacus
spots.summary: Hercules and Cacus is an Italian Renaissance sculpture in marble to the right of the entrance of the Palazzo Vecchio in the Piazza della Signoria, Florence, Italy.

spots.name: Boboli Gardens
spots.summary: The Boboli Gardens is a large park in Florence, originally designed as the garden of the Medici family's Pitti Palace in the mid-16th century. It is an important early Italian garden which influenced aristocratic gardens across Europe.

spots.name: North Doors of the Florence Baptistery
spots.summary: The North Doors of the Florence Baptistery were made by Lorenzo Ghiberti between 1403 and 1424 and represent his first masterpiece, before the celebrated Gates of Paradise.
spots.wikipediaTitle: North Doors of the Florence Baptistery

spots.name: Palazzo Strozzi

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Palazzo Strozzi is a palace in Florence, Italy. It is located in the historic centre between the homonymous Via Strozzi and Piazza Strozzi, and Via Tornabuoni.

spots.name: San Miniato al Monte

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: San Miniato al Monte is a basilica in Florence, central Italy, standing atop one of the highest points in the city. It has been described as one of the finest Romanesque structures in Tuscany and one of the most scenic churches in Italy.

spots.name: Medici lions
spots.summary: The Medici lions are a pair of marble sculptures of lions: one of which is Roman, dating to the 2nd century AD, and the other a 16th-century pendant. By 1598 both were placed at the Villa Medici, Rome. Since 1789 they have been displayed at the Loggia dei Lanzi in Florence.

spots.name: Santa Reparata, Florence

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Santa Reparata is the former cathedral of Florence, Italy. Its name refers to Saint Reparata, an early virgin martyr who is the co-patron saint of Florence. Florence Cathedral was constructed over it.

spots.name: Ognissanti, Florence

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The chiesa di San Salvatore di Ognissanti, or more simply chiesa di Ognissanti, is a Franciscan church located on the eponymous piazza in central Florence, region of Tuscany, Italy. Founded by the lay order of the Umiliati, the church was dedicated to all saints and martyrs, known and unknown.

spots.name: Porcellino
spots.summary: The Porcellino (transl. "Piglet") is the local Florentine nickname for the bronze fountain of a boar.

spots.name: Wrestlers
spots.summary: The Wrestlers is a Roman marble sculpture after a lost Greek original of the third century BCE. It is now in the Uffizi collection in Florence, Italy.

spots.name: Laurentian Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Laurentian Library is a historic library in Florence, Italy, containing more than 11,000 manuscripts and 4,500 early printed books.

spots.name: Museum of San Marco
spots.summary: Museo Nazionale di San Marco is an art museum housed in the monumental section of the medieval Dominican convent of San Marco dedicated to St Mark, situated on the present-day Piazza San Marco, in Florence, a region of Tuscany, Italy.

spots.name: Pasquino Group
spots.summary: The Pasquino Group is a group of marble sculptures that copy a Hellenistic bronze original, dating to ca. 200–150 BCE. At least fifteen Roman marble copies of this sculpture are known.

spots.name: Studiolo of Francesco I

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Studiolo is a small painting-encrusted barrel-vaulted room in the Palazzo Vecchio, Florence, Italy. It was commissioned by Francesco I de' Medici, Grand Duke of Tuscany.

spots.name: Equestrian Monument of Cosimo I
spots.summary: The Equestrian Monument of Cosimo I is a bronze equestrian statue executed by Giambologna from 1587 to 1594, and erected in 1594 in the Piazza della Signoria in Florence, Tuscany, Italy.

spots.name: Tomb of Antipope John XXIII
spots.summary: The marble-and-bronze tomb monument of Antipope John XXIII was created by Donatello and Michelozzo for the Florence Baptistry adjacent to the Duomo.

spots.name: Sagrestia Nuova

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sagrestia Nuova, also known as the New Sacristy and the Medici Chapel, is a mausoleum that stands as a testament to the grandeur and artistic vision of the Medici family. Constructed in 1520, the mausoleum was designed by the Italian artist and architect Michelangelo.

spots.name: Pazzi Chapel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Pazzi Chapel is a chapel located in the "first cloister" on the southern flank of the Basilica di Santa Croce in Florence, Italy. Commonly credited to Filippo Brunelleschi, it is considered to be one of the masterpieces of Renaissance architecture.

spots.name: Saint George
spots.summary: Saint George is a marble sculpture by Donatello currently housed in the Bargello Museum in Florence, Italy. It is one of fourteen sculptures commissioned by the guilds of Florence to decorate the external niches of the Orsanmichele Church.

spots.name: Santo Spirito

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica di Santo Spirito is a church in Florence, Italy. Usually referred to simply as Santo Spirito, it is located in the Oltrarno quarter, facing the square with the same name. The interior of the building – internal length 97 m (318 ft) – is one of the preeminent examples of Renaissance architecture.

spots.name: Piazza della Repubblica
spots.summary: Piazza della Repubblica is a city square in Florence, Italy.

spots.name: Galleria Palatina

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Palazzo Pitti, in English sometimes called the Pitti Palace, is a vast, mainly in the Renaissance style, palace in Florence, Italy. It is situated on the south side of the River Arno, a short distance from the Ponte Vecchio.

spots.name: Loggia del Mercato Nuovo

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Loggia del Mercato Nuovo, popularly known as the Loggia del Porcellino, is a building in Florence, Italy. It is so called to distinguish it from the Mercato vecchio that used to be located in the area of today's Piazza della Repubblica.

spots.name: Officina di Santa Maria Novella
spots.summary: The Officina Profumo-Farmaceutica di Santa Maria Novella, also known as the Pharmacy of Santa Maria Novella or the Ancient Apothecary of Santa Maria Novella, is an Italian company active in the fields of perfumery, cosmetics and herbal products, based at Via della Scala 16 in Florence, within the historic premises of the convent complex of the Basilica of Santa Maria Novella.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Officina Profumo-Farmaceutica di Santa Maria Novella

spots.name: Badia Fiorentina

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Badìa Fiorentina is an abbey and church now home to the Monastic Communities of Jerusalem situated on the Via del Proconsolo in the centre of Florence, Italy. Dante supposedly grew up across the street in what is now called the Casa di Dante, rebuilt in 1910 as a museum to Dante.

spots.name: Santa Trinita

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Santa Trinita is a Roman Catholic church located in front of the piazza of the same name, traversed by Via de' Tornabuoni, in central Florence, Tuscany, Italy. It is the mother church of the Vallumbrosan Order of Monks, founded in 1092 by a Florentine nobleman.

spots.name: Villa La Petraia
spots.summary: Villa La Petraia is one of the Medici villas in Castello, Florence, Tuscany, central Italy. It has a distinctive 19th-century belvedere on the upper east terrace on axis with the view of Florence.

spots.name: Ponte Santa Trinita
spots.summary: The Ponte Santa Trinita is a Renaissance bridge in Florence, Italy, spanning the Arno. The Ponte Santa Trìnita is the oldest elliptic arch bridge in the world, characterised by three flattened ellipses. The outside spans each measure 29 m (95 ft) with the centre span being 32 m (105 ft) in length.

spots.name: Palazzo Rucellai

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Palazzo Rucellai is a palatial fifteenth-century townhouse on the Via della Vigna Nuova in Florence, Italy. The Rucellai Palace is believed by most scholars to have been designed for Giovanni di Paolo Rucellai by Leon Battista Alberti between 1446 and 1451 and executed, at least in part, by Bernardo Rossellino.

spots.name: Loggia del Bigallo

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Loggia del Bigallo is a late Gothic building in Florence, region of Tuscany, Italy. It stands at the corner of Piazza San Giovanni and via Calzaioli; tradition holds the site near the Baptistry of Florence was donated by a benefactor.
